title: Length of her stay in Chicago
summary: She arrived spring 1925 and left October or November to be home for her grandmother's birthday.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Did he travel out on the road with any band or anything while you were gone? No. He went around Chicago, that's about how I was there. No, he went around Chicago, yes. He stayed there.
And things were kind of a quiet thing, you know, it was peacetime. There wasn't too much money in circulation.
No, no, that was in the summer of when, about 1925 you went?
I went in the spring of 1925, right after all the snow was up, because he didn't want me to come during that winter. He was sick that winter, but he didn't want me to come. He didn't want me to come.
And sick that winter before, early in 1925.

And I wanted to graduate with my beauty culture class. So I had to come back home for hair dressing and... I was a manicurist then, working the daytime and going to school at night. You stayed there almost a whole year then? Yes, indeed. And in fact, when he thought when the weather was getting too cool for me to stay up there, he wanted me to come home because I wasn't used to the North, he said. It would be too cold on me.
But you did stay in that winter, that next winter then? No, I didn't stay the whole winter. It got too cold, no.
I just stayed the whole winter. I got there early spring and I left there about October or November. I wanted to be home for my grandmother's birthday the 1st of November. Oh.
